activities.text: Priya: we need solid auth for project orbit. The REST API needs token issuing and refresh. You own the auth module, please drive it.
activities.speaker: human
owner
activities.text: Plan: implement POST /login, GET /me, POST /logout on Postgres session table. Then add tests for login, expiry, and logout. Will keep tokens opaque for now.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Sounds good. Grabbed coffee, by the way the office espresso machine is finally fixed.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Decision: to keep login fast I will store session tokens in Redis with a 24h TTL. Lookup is a single GET and expiry is automatic.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text:
auth-api v1:
POST /login accepts {username, password}.
On success returns 200 {token, expires_in}.
token is an opaque bearer token.
expires_in is seconds until expiry (3600).
POST /logout accepts {token} and revokes it.
GET /me requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.
All responses are JSON with {data} or {error}.
Errors use 401 for bad credentials, 403 for expired.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Nit: login handler looks fine, just rename `tok` to `token` for readability. No functional issue.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Objection: Redis eviction can silently drop active sessions. With allkeys-lru and no persistence, a restart logs out everyone and we lose revocation audit. Use Postgres as authority.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Agreed, switching. We will store session tokens in Postgres with row-level expiry. Redis will only be an optional read cache, never authoritative.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Quick question: what TTL are we using for access tokens? 15 minutes or an hour?

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: TTL call: access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Short window limits damage if a token leaks. Refresh will come later with a longer window.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Hypothetical: what if we went fully stateless JWT with no server store? Just thinking out loud, not asking to change anything now.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Implemented POST /refresh (no rotation yet). It takes the old access token, issues a new one. No locking yet, single UPDATE query.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Objection: login handler logs the full bearer token at info level. Please do not log raw tokens anywhere; log only a sha256 prefix of 8 chars for debugging.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Fixed logging: redacted token field, now logs token_prefix only. Grepped codebase, no other raw token prints.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Added per-user refresh lock with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the session row. Concurrent refresh now serializes and issues exactly one token.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Standup note: auth is on track, demo is Thursday. No action needed.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Weekend plans aside, I re-ran login tests locally and they pass. Nice work on the lock fix.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: New requirement: mobile clients need long sessions. Please add a refresh_token to the contract so they can renew without re-login.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Proposal: v2 adds refresh_token with rotation. POST /login returns both tokens, POST /refresh consumes the old refresh token and returns a new pair.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Objection: rotation without reuse detection is unsafe. If an attacker replays an old refresh token we must reject reused refresh tokens and revoke the whole family.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text:
auth-api v2:
POST /login accepts {username, password}.
On success returns 200 {token, refresh_token, expires_in}.
token is a short-lived bearer token, expires_in 900.
refresh_token is a one-time long-lived token, 7 days.
POST /refresh accepts {refresh_token}.
On success returns 200 {token, refresh_token, expires_in}.
Reuse of a rotated refresh_token returns 401 and revokes family.
GET /me requires Authorization: Bearer <token>.
POST /logout accepts {refresh_token} and revokes the family.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Implemented v2: we rotate refresh tokens on every use and reject reuse. Reuse triggers family revoke plus 401. Covered by test_refresh_rotation and test_refresh_reuse.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Rollout plan: 1) merge v2, 2) migrate sessions, 3) update mobile docs. Tracking in issue ORB-214.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Note for newcomers: we used to store tokens in Redis before the Postgres switch, do not copy that pattern. Postgres is authoritative now.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Added fast-path refresh for v2 mobile clients. It bypasses the lock for speed, single UPDATE without SELECT FOR UPDATE. Should be fine, tests pass locally.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Reminder for the docs: auth-api v1 returned only {token, expires_in} with no refresh_token. That is obsolete, current v2 always returns refresh_token on login.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Heads up: some v1 clients still send expires_in, ignore them. Server must not trust client expiry, always use server-side expiry and v2 refresh_token flow.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Proposal: drop refresh_token and go back to auth-api v1 for simplicity. One token is easier to debug. Requesting approval to revert.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Rejected: keep v2 with refresh_token. Mobile needs long sessions and reuse detection. Do not revert to v1.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Coffee break: anyone tried the new place downstairs? Back in 10.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Fixed fast-path: restored acquire per-user lock before refreshing tokens. All refresh paths now do SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, no lock-free shortcut.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Confirming: Postgres remains the authoritative token store. Redis is disabled for auth reads until further notice.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Confirming lifetimes: access tokens 15 min, refresh tokens expire after 7 days with rotation. Family revoke on reuse stays in force.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Final state: v2 login returns token plus refresh_token, rotation with reuse revoke, per-user lock on every refresh, Postgres authority, no raw token logs.

lessons.statement: Acquire per-user lock before refreshing tokens; lock-free refresh issues duplicate tokens and fails the race test.
Never log raw bearer tokens; log only a short hash prefix.
Reject reused refresh tokens and revoke the whole token family on replay.
